message.content:
**Plasma‑Membrane Proteins – A Quick Overview** | Category | Typical Function | Representative Examples | |----------|------------------|------------------------| | **Integral (Transmembrane) Proteins** | Span the lipid bilayer; often act as channels, pumps, carriers, or receptors. | • Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase
• Glucose transporter GLUT1
• Aquaporin‑2 (water pore)
• G‑protein–coupled receptors (e.g., β₂‑adrenergic receptor)
• Ionotropic glutamate receptors (NMDA, AMPA)
• Connexin hemichannels (Cx43)
• Integrin αβ heterodimers (α5β1, αvβ3) | | **Peripheral Membrane Proteins** | Associate loosely with one side of the membrane through electrostatic interactions or short hydrophobic patches. | • Annexins (bind phospholipids when Ca²⁺ present)
• Caveolin‑1 (scaffold protein in caveolae)
• Band‑7 domain proteins (flotillins) | | **Lipid‑Anchored Proteins** | Covalently attached to lipids embedded in the outer leaflet. | • GPI‑anchored glycoproteins (CD59, Thyroglobulin)
• Palmitoylated Ras family members (HRas, KRas) | | **Extracellular Matrix / Adhesion Molecules** | Mediate cell–matrix or cell–cell adhesion. | • Cadherins (E‑cadherin, N‑cadherin)
• Selectins (P-, E-selectin)
• Neural Cell Adhesion Molecule (NCAM) | ### Key Points About Plasma-Membrane Protein Composition 1. **Diversity & Complexity** - Roughly 30% of all human genes encode membrane proteins—far more than once thought. - These proteins constitute ~50% of drug targets due to their accessibility. 2. **Structural Motifs** - *Alpha-helical* transmembrane domains dominate (~70%) in mammals. - *Beta-barrels* are typical of bacterial outer membranes and mitochondria/chloroplast inner membranes rather than mammalian plasma membranes. 3. **Functional Classes** - **Transporters/Pumps:** Move ions/metabolites across the membrane (e.g., Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase, CFTR chloride channel). - **Receptors:** Detect extracellular signals (GPCRs, tyrosine kinase receptors like EGFR). - **Channels:** Permit passive ion flow (voltage-gated K⁺ channels, TRPV1 nociceptor). - **Adhesion Molecules:** Facilitate intercellular contacts (integrins, cadherins). 4. **Post‑translational Modifications** - Many plasma-membrane proteins undergo palmitoylation, myristoylation, or prenylation to anchor them into the lipid bilayer. - Glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) anchors attach certain proteins exclusively to the outer leaflet. --- #### How to Find Specific Proteins Programmatically If you’d like a curated list pulled directly from databases: ```python from functions import cellbio_get_proteins result = cellbio_get_proteins({ "cell_compartment": "plasma_membrane", "include_description": True }) print(result) ``` *(This would retrieve a comprehensive set of known plasma‑membrane proteins along with optional descriptions.)* Feel free to let me know if you’re interested in particular subclasses (e.g., GPCR families), species-specific listings, or functional annotations!
